account:
Frozen facts used: tree rooted at v0; non-root children are mutations of a,b,c; child max ≤4d³ (answer:work:003-struct-core-v2, answer:work:004-upper-depth-v3).
L1. For j≥1, d0=1,d1=3,c_j=d_{j-1}; v0=(1,1,1,1), v_j=(1,1,c_j,d_j). Induction/mutation gives 2+c_j²+d_j²=4c_jd_j and d_{j+1}=4d_j−d_{j−1}. λ=2+√3; d_j=Aλ^j+Bλ^{−j}, A=(3+√3)/6, B=(3−√3)/6. Since A+Bλ^{−2j}≤A+B=1, d_j≤λ^j; d_j strictly increases, so N(H)≥⌊log_λH⌋+1.
L2. Child maximum f(x)=4abcd/x−x is strictly decreasing, so distinct values among a,b,c give distinct children. If a=b=c=x, d²=x²(4xd−3), so x|d; d=kx gives k²+3=4kx², hence k|3. k=1→v0; k=3→v1=(1,1,1,3). Thus depth≥2⇒≥2 distinct children.
L3. From v2=(1,1,3,11), A=log₂11+1. Each edge gives L+1≤3(L+1), so after t edges log₂d≤3^tA. If 3^tA≤log₂H, the 2^t level-t vertices below v2 have d≤H. Take t=⌊log₃(log₂H/A)⌋, β=log₃2=0.6309, c′=1/(2A^β)≈0.194, H≥32; then N(H)≥2^t≥c′(log₂H)^β.
FINAL: N(H)≥max{⌊log_{2+√3}H⌋+1, c′(log₂H)^0.6309} for H≥32. Correction: the first term is asymptotically dominant (1>0.6309). CONJECTURE stronger than Θ(log H): missing positive-density branching/typical-growth lemma.
assumptions: Vertices are sorted quadruples with permutations identified; height is the maximum coordinate d.
The structural tree/child facts are cited as frozen from answer:work:003-struct-core-v2 and answer:work:004-upper-depth-v3, not reproved here.
No blocked lower-bound answer is used as evidence.

boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: The memorandum would state a false asymptotic comparison despite a correct two-term lower bound; the correction preserves the bound and separates the false dominance claim.
boundary_findings.narrative: The assigned final-line clause asserts that the polylogarithmic term c'(log2 H)^0.6309 is asymptotically dominant, but the proved chain term is Theta(log H) and dominates it.

citations.excerpt: quotient graph is a rooted tree; mutating a,b,c raises height

claims.statement: Frozen facts used without reproof: the sorted mutation graph is a tree rooted at (1,1,1,1); at a non-root the children are the distinct sorted mutations of a,b,c; every child maximum is at most 4d^3.

L1: the chain v_j=(1,1,d_{j-1},d_j), d0=1,d1=3,d_{j+1}=4d_j-d_{j-1}, consists of distinct solutions; with lambda=2+sqrt(3), d_j=A lambda^j+B lambda^{-j}, A=(3+sqrt3)/6, B=(3-sqrt3)/6, hence d_j<=lambda^j and N(H)>=floor(log_lambda H)+1.

citations.excerpt: children of a non-root are the distinct sorted vertices obtained by mutating a,b,c

claims.statement: L2: every vertex at depth at least 2 has at least two distinct children: f(x)=4abcd/x-x is strictly decreasing, and the equal case a=b=c=x forces x|d, d=kx, k^2+3=4kx^2, k|3, giving only the root or (1,1,1,3).

counterevidence: The assignment's clause that the (log H)^0.6309 term is asymptotically dominant is false: it is o(log H).
claims.statement: L3 and final bound: below v2=(1,1,3,11), with A=log2(11)+1, after t edges log2 d<=3^t A; for t=floor(log_3(log2(H)/A)), beta=log_3 2=0.6309, c'=1/(2A^beta) approximately 0.194, H>=32, N(H)>=c'(log2 H)^beta. Therefore N(H)>=max{floor(log_{2+sqrt3}H)+1, c'(log2 H)^0.6309}; the logarithmic chain term is asymptotically dominant.

counterevidence: Dominance clause in the packet is incorrect: floor(log_{2+sqrt3} H)+1 = Theta(log H), while c'(log2 H)^0.6309 = Theta((log H)^0.6309), and 1>0.6309.
The worst-case edge estimate child max <=4d^3 caps the proved binary-subtree exponent at log_3 2<1; exceeding Theta(log H) requires typical-growth control, not this worst-case estimate.

knowledge_links.rationale: Provides L1, L2, L3, the explicit constants lambda, beta, A, c', threshold H>=32, and the final two-term lower bound, while correcting the false dominance clause.
Establishes the strongest currently proved lower bound in this packet: N(H)>=max{floor(log_{2+sqrt3}H)+1, c'(log2 H)^0.6309} for H>=32.
Completes the same lower-bound demand independently; no blocked lower-bound answer is cited as evidence.
Completes the retry demand with explicit proofs of L1-L3 and labels all stronger growth as conjectural.

raised_questions.acceptance_condition: Either prove N(H)>=(log H)^{1+delta} for an explicit delta>0 with constants, or prove that along all but o(depth) levels the two-child branches have average log-growth slope 3, blocking this route.
discriminating_outcomes: Positive delta with explicit constants: the branching term exceeds Theta(log H).
Average slope 3 on almost all levels: the 4d^3 worst case is typical for branching, so a new invariant or family is required.
raised_questions.rationale: The binary-subtree argument is limited by the worst-case estimate child max<=4d^3, whose level-t height bound is 3^t A and yields only 2^t=(log H)^{log_3 2}; surpassing Theta(log H) requires typical, not worst-case, growth control.
raised_questions.text: Can the lower bound be pushed beyond Theta(log H)? Prove or refute that inside subtree(v2) a positive-density set of vertices has two children with average log-growth slope strictly below 3 over Omega(depth) consecutive levels, yielding N(H)>=(log H)^{1+delta} for some delta>0.

unresolved: Any lower bound stronger than Theta(log H), e.g. N(H)>=(log H)^{1+delta}, remains conjectural; the exact missing lemma is positive-density two-child branching with average log-growth slope strictly below 3 over Omega(depth) levels.
The gap to the proved upper bound N(H)=O(H^{ln3/ln11}) remains large and is not addressed by this lower-bound packet.
